item.title: French blood banks targeted by refrigerator cyberattack
item.description:
Another wave of cyberattacks against European supermarkets this week compromised refrigeration systems for the second time in a month, rekindling fears over the security of critical infrastructure. While such attacks so far have been costly and inconvenient , a new era of AI-enabled cyberwarfare could portend more devastating disruptions. France’s national blood service, which 1,900 hospitals rely on, said Tuesday that hackers raised the temperature at cold storage units , but the attack was thwarted before any damage was done . Experts frequently blame Russia for such incidents: Many Kremlin-aligned hacks are unsophisticated, but “the problem is that the more they poke around, the more it is probable they can find something critical that wasn’t protected well ,” a cyber analyst said. — Brendan Ruberry

item.title: Gina Hinojosa won the governor’s race. What happens to Texas data centers now?
item.description:
Texas Democratic gubernatorial candidate, State Rep. Gina Hinojosa waits to speak during a Block Walk midterm campaign rally in San Antonio, Texas, on November 1, 2026. —Brandon Bell—Getty Images Republican Texas Gov. Greg Abbott has been defeated by Democratic gubernatorial candidate and state Gina Hinojosa, a stunning loss that marks the end of a long streak of GOP leadership in the state. Texas has been led by Republican governors since 1995, when George W. Bush defeated then incumbent Democratic Gov. Ann Richards . Richards was the last Democrat to win a governor’s race in the state, in 1990. Hinojosa will also become the first Hispanic governor to lead Texas, which hosts the largest Latino population in the United States. The AP called the race for Hinojosa Tuesday night. During a concession speech Tuesday night, Abbott said that he had congratulated Hinojosa and thanked his staff…
